rule: accumulated MIXED Track-B channels, ranked by |alone-AUC - .5| on FIT+MINE only
selected_parents: Enumeration count of evaluation settings and resource markers
Extent of coverage listing and breadth vocabulary
Density of formal vocabulary and mathematical notation on the page

candidates.criterion: Count of enumerated evaluation settings and resource markers
candidates.instruction: Score 0-10 by counting or estimating how many distinct evaluation settings and resource markers the abstract enumerates. Count mentions of: named or counted datasets or benchmarks; tasks; languages; domains; model architectures or model families; model sizes or parameter counts; transfer, zero-shot, or cross-lingual settings; numbers of baselines compared; and explicit scale statements such as compute used, number of runs, or number of human raters. 0 = the abstract names no evaluation setting at all. 2 = one setting is named. 5 = roughly three or four distinct settings or counts are named. 8 = five to eight are named, or explicit large counts appear. 10 = the abstract enumerates many settings, or states large counts across several of these categories. This is explicitly NOT a quality judgement. Do not decide whether the coverage is adequate, necessary, convincing, or excessive; do not consider whether anything informative was learned in those settings; do not consider whether the comparisons were controlled. Score only how much enumeration is present in the text.
candidates.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Evaluation breadth

candidates.instruction: Rate from 0 to 10 how much the abstract contains theorem, proof, bound, assumption, equation, or mathematically formal terminology; judge formalism extent only, not rigor, correctness, or research value.

Score 0-10 how many currently-fashionable subfield buzzwords appear in the abstract (e.g., 'GPT', 'in-context learning', 'diffusion', 'Transformer', 'large language model', 'foundation model'). 0 = no such terms appear; 10 = the abstract is dense with such terms throughout. Do not judge whether the use of these terms is warranted, accurate, or central to the contribution -- score only the raw presence of this vocabulary.

candidates.criterion: Enumeration count of evaluation settings and resource markers
candidates.instruction: Score 0-10 by counting or estimating how many distinct evaluation settings and resource markers the text enumerates, and nothing else. Count each of: named or counted datasets or benchmarks; named tasks; named languages; named domains; named model architectures or model families; model sizes or parameter counts; transfer, zero-shot, few-shot, or cross-lingual settings named as settings; a stated number of baselines or comparison systems; and explicit scale statements such as compute used, GPU-hours, number of training runs or seeds, number of human annotators, or corpus size. 0 = no evaluation setting or resource marker of any kind is named. 2 = exactly one is named. 5 = roughly three or four distinct settings or counts appear. 8 = five to eight appear, or an explicit large count appears (for example 'twelve benchmarks'). 10 = many appear, or large counts appear across several of these categories at once. This is explicitly NOT a quality judgement. Do not decide whether the coverage is adequate, necessary, convincing, redundant, or excessive; do not consider whether anything was learned in those settings; do not consider whether the comparisons were controlled or fair; do not consider whether the claim is supported. If an item lists many settings and reports no finding at all, it must still be able to score 10. Score only the amount of enumeration present on the page.
candidates.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Count of enumerated evaluation settings and resource markers

candidates.criterion: Extent of formal notation and mathematical vocabulary
candidates.instruction: Score 0-10 the raw extent of mathematically formal vocabulary and notation in the abstract text. Count or estimate the presence of: words such as theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary, proof, bound, convergence, rate, assumption, regularity, convexity, optimality, complexity, and similar formal-mathematical vocabulary; and any inline mathematical notation such as Greek letters, single-letter variable names, subscripts or superscripts, norms, expectations, probability symbols, big-O expressions, inequalities, or displayed formulas. 0 = the abstract contains none of these markers at all. 3 = one or two isolated markers. 7 = markers recur in several sentences. 10 = the abstract is dense with such vocabulary and notation from start to finish. This is explicitly NOT a quality judgement. Do not consider whether the formalism is correct, rigorous, necessary, well used, or informative; do not consider whether the paper actually proves anything; do not consider whether the notation is defined. Score only how much of this vocabulary and notation is present on the page.
candidates.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Formalism density

candidates.criterion: Extent of coverage listing and breadth vocabulary
candidates.instruction: Score 0-10 by counting or estimating how much the text lists coverage and how much breadth-signalling vocabulary it uses. Count two things together: (i) the number of listed datasets, benchmarks, tasks, domains, languages, model architectures, model sizes, baselines, or experimental settings, whether named individually or given as a count ('twelve benchmarks', 'six languages'); and (ii) occurrences of breadth-signalling phrasing such as extensive experiments, comprehensive evaluation, a wide range of, across diverse, large-scale, multilingual, cross-domain, cross-lingual, zero-shot, in-the-wild, at scale, or thorough ablations. 0 = the text lists no coverage items and uses no such phrasing. 3 = one or two items or one such phrase. 6 = several listed items, or a coverage phrase plus a short list. 10 = long enumeration across multiple categories, or several breadth phrases stacked together, or both. This is explicitly NOT a quality judgement. Do not decide whether the listed coverage is adequate, appropriate, persuasive, redundant, or padded; do not consider whether the conditions differ in any meaningful way; do not consider whether any result across them is reported; do not consider whether the breadth vocabulary is warranted. An item that lists a dozen benchmarks and reports only 'consistently outperforms' must still be able to score 10.
candidates.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Evaluation-breadth signaling

candidates.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the text lists many datasets, tasks, domains, architectures, baselines, or experimental settings; judge the breadth of enumeration only, not whether the evaluation is adequate or persuasive.

candidates.criterion: Density of formal vocabulary and mathematical notation on the page
candidates.instruction: Score 0-10 for the raw extent of formal-mathematical vocabulary and notation in the text, counting or estimating only. Count occurrences of formal-mathematical vocabulary such as theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary, proof, bound, convergence, rate, assumption, regularity, convexity, smoothness, optimality, minimax, complexity, estimator, guarantee, and close relatives; and any inline notation such as Greek letters, single-letter variable names, subscripts or superscripts, norms, expectations, probability symbols, big-O or Omega expressions, inequalities, set or operator symbols, or displayed formulas. 0 = none of these markers appears anywhere. 3 = one or two isolated markers in the whole text. 7 = markers recur across several sentences. 10 = such vocabulary and notation are dense from the first sentence to the last. This is explicitly NOT a quality judgement. Do not consider whether the formalism is correct, rigorous, necessary, well used, or informative; do not consider whether anything is actually proved; do not consider whether symbols are defined or whether assumptions are stated; do not consider whether the prose is clear. An item saturated with symbols that states nothing a reader could check must still be able to score 10.
candidates.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Extent of formal notation and mathematical vocabulary

candidates.instruction: Rate from 0 to 10 how much the abstract claims coverage across multiple datasets, languages, domains, tasks, architectures, or transfer settings; judge breadth of described coverage only, not whether it is adequate or convincing.
Score 0-10 for how much the abstract uses theorem, proof, bound, convergence, asymptotic, or formal mathematical-guarantee language; judge only extent, not correctness or importance.

Score 0-10 for how much the abstract uses equations, asymptotic notation, named theorems, proofs, bounds, optimization conditions, or other formal mathematical language; judge amount only, not whether the formalism is rigorous or valuable.
How much does the abstract name canonical datasets, benchmarks, architectures, standard methods, or well-known prior authors? Score only visible ecosystem references, not the importance of the work.

Score 0-10 for the extent to which the abstract advertises code, models, configuration files, datasets, videos, or other reproducibility resources; judge only the presence and prominence of these signals, never their usefulness.
candidates.upstream_parent: author's reproducibility practice and available resources

candidates.criterion: Density of specific quantified result figures
candidates.instruction: Rate 0-10 the density of explicitly quantified outcome figures in the text. Count numerals attached to results: percentages, absolute metric values (accuracy, AP, mIoU, FID, MAE), speedup or reduction factors (for example five-fold, two to three orders of magnitude), parameter, FLOP or batch-size counts, wall-clock times, and dataset sizes. Anchors: 0 = no such numerals anywhere; 3 = one figure; 5 = two or three; 8 = four or five; 10 = six or more distinct quantified figures, several carried to one or two decimal places. Score PRESENCE AND DENSITY of numbers only. Do not assess whether the numbers are large, impressive, fairly compared, correctly computed, or whether the gains would matter to anyone.

Rate from 0 to 10 how much the abstract advertises code, pretrained models, datasets, repositories, or reproducibility artifacts; judge the presence of availability statements only, not whether the artifacts are useful or the research is sound.

Score 0-10 for the extent of explicit language promising or linking code, models, datasets, configurations, or other research artifacts; judge only the presence of release signaling, not whether the artifacts are useful or real.

Score how many specific, checkable numeric results (percentages, deltas, counts, timings) the abstract reports, independent of how positive or well-supported they are. A 10 packs multiple precise figures (e.g., '10.9% improvement', '5-fold reduction', '76 minutes'). A 0 reports only qualitative adjectives ('significant', 'considerable', 'remarkable') with no numbers at all.

Score 0-10 how explicitly the abstract states that code, data, or trained models will be or are being released (e.g., a repository URL, 'code is available at...', 'we release our implementation'). 0 = no release statement of any kind; 10 = an explicit, specific release statement naming a repository. Do not judge whether releasing code says anything about the work's quality -- score only whether the statement is textually present.

candidates.criterion: Density of quantified benchmark results in text
candidates.instruction: Rate 0-10 the density of concrete quantitative results stated in the abstract: numerals, percentage gains, absolute metric values, benchmark deltas, parameter counts, FLOP counts, speedup factors and named leaderboard figures. 0 = no numbers reported at all; 3 = one vague quantified claim; 6 = two or three precise figures; 10 = many precise figures woven through several sentences. Count how much quantified reporting is present on the surface. Do not judge whether the numbers are large, impressive, credible, correctly obtained or well chosen, and do not reward or penalise the absence of numbers.

Score whether the abstract explicitly states that code, models, or data will be or are publicly released. A 10 states a concrete release (e.g., a GitHub link or explicit 'code is available'). A 0 makes no mention of release or reproducibility artifacts.

Score from 0 (absent) to 10 (highly prominent) the extent to which the abstract contains an explicit URL to a code repository (e.g., GitHub) or explicitly states that code is open-sourced. Do not judge the quality or usefulness of the code, only the presence of the repository mention.
Score 0-10 for how much the abstract introduces named methods, abbreviations, and component labels; judge only extent, not whether the naming is useful or technically good.

On a 0-10 scale, rate ONLY how much the text names concrete large-scale infrastructure or resource figures (specific hardware such as 'TPU Pod', specific huge batch sizes or wall-clock training-time claims, or explicit counts of baselines/search-spaces/datasets used in a single study), where 0 = no such resource/scale figures and 10 = multiple specific large-scale resource figures are named. Do NOT judge whether the scale achieved is impressive or whether more compute makes better research; score only the presence of named resource/scale figures.
candidates.upstream_parent: author's institutional resources / access to large-scale compute or experimental infrastructure

candidates.criterion: Sheer expository volume of the abstract body
candidates.instruction: Read only the abstract text and rate 0-10 how much total expository volume is present. Anchors: 0 = title only, or a single sentence of body text; 3 = roughly two to four sentences; 6 = one standard paragraph of about eight to twelve sentences; 10 = a long multi-part abstract of fifteen or more sentences covering several elaborated sub-topics. Count sentences, clauses, enumerated sub-points and number of distinct sub-topics touched. You are measuring QUANTITY OF TEXT ONLY. Do not judge whether the length is appropriate, whether the writing is clear or informative, or whether a short abstract is terse-and-confident versus thin. Longer is not better and shorter is not better; report extent only.

On a 0-10 scale, rate ONLY how long and elaborated the abstract text is (word count, number of sub-clauses/sub-claims covered), where 0 = extremely terse (roughly one to two sentences, under ~60 words) and 10 = extremely long and elaborated (many clauses and sub-claims, over ~250 words). Do NOT judge whether the length is appropriate or whether the underlying work is good; score length alone.
Rate from 0 (very brief) to 10 (very long) how much text, sentence count, and elaboration the abstract contains; judge extent only, not whether the additional detail is good or useful.

candidates.criterion: Crowded-field late-synthesis vs first-mover idea framing
candidates.instruction: On a 0-10 scale, rate ONLY how much the abstract frames itself as arriving late into an already-crowded space of many named/enumerated prior alternatives that it must position against, unify, or amalgamate (e.g., 'Existing methods have attempted...', 'Many...have been proposed...however none...', 'amalgamate a pool of teacher optimizers'), versus reading as a direct, minimally-contrastive presentation of one self-contained new idea. Score 0 = reads as a first, direct, minimally-contrastive presentation of an idea; 10 = reads as a late synthesis/differentiation move that explicitly catalogues and positions against many prior alternatives. Do NOT judge whether the positioning against prior work is accurate or whether the synthesis is a genuine advance; score only how much the framing reads as 'early direct idea' vs 'late crowded-field synthesis'.
candidates.upstream_parent: position in the entry stream — how many similar prior submissions/approaches already existed when this abstract was framed

candidates.instruction: Score 0-10 for the extent of fluent grammar, consistent terminology, smooth transitions, and carefully standardized prose; judge only textual polish, not research quality.

How much does the abstract exhibit highly polished grammar, smooth transitions, standardized abstract structure, and publication-template fluency? Score only surface editing quality, not research quality.

candidates.criterion: Inline mathematical notation and complexity-bound density
candidates.instruction: Score how much of the abstract's visible surface is occupied by inline mathematical notation rather than prose: LaTeX-style symbols and macros, named spaces and sets, big-O or order expressions, epsilon / delta / d / k / H parameters, subscripted or superscripted variables, and bracketed theory-venue citations such as [Author, VENUE'yy]. Score 0 if there is no notation at all and the abstract is entirely prose; score 5 if notation appears occasionally, for example one complexity expression or a couple of symbols; score 10 if notation appears in most sentences and a reader must parse formulas to follow the claims. Count the notation on the page. The judge must NOT judge rigour, correctness, difficulty, or whether formalism is warranted for this topic, and must not treat notation as evidence either for or against the work being good.
candidates.upstream_parent: writing conventions of the theory-versus-applied subcommunity that produced the work

candidates.instruction: Read the abstract text only. Rate 0-10 how much specialized mathematical/symbolic notation appears (inline formulas, Greek letters, subscripts/superscripts, big-O/tilde-O expressions, set/space notation like R^d). Score 0 if the text is plain prose with no symbolic notation, and 10 if the text is dense with symbolic expressions throughout. Do NOT judge whether the mathematics is correct, rigorous, or important -- score only how much symbolic notation is visibly present in the text.

candidates.criterion: Rhetorical framing as adjudicating a field debate
candidates.instruction: Score whether the abstract explicitly frames itself as resolving an open question or tension in prior literature, using a direct question or an explicit 'prior work suggests X, but...' setup, versus simply stating 'we propose method M for task T' without any such framing device. A 10 opens with an explicit posed question or named tension the paper will resolve. A 0 states its contribution directly with no debate-framing device.

Score 10 if the architecture is derived directly from first principles, such as continuous ordinary/partial differential equations or dynamical systems. Score 0 if the architecture is constructed by stacking discrete heuristic blocks based solely on empirical performance.

Read the abstract text only. Rate 0-10 how strongly the text makes an explicit claim to being first, novel-in-priority, or unprecedented (e.g., 'we are the first to...', 'for the first time', 'to the best of our knowledge, ... is the first'). Score 0 if no such priority claim appears, and 10 if the text makes an emphatic, explicit priority claim. Do NOT judge whether the priority claim is actually true or historically accurate -- score only whether this rhetorical claim is textually present.

candidates.criterion: Enumerated contribution scaffolding and roadmap phrasing
candidates.instruction: Score how much explicit enumerated scaffolding the abstract uses to present its contributions: phrases such as 'our contributions are three-fold' or 'two-fold', sequences of 'First, ... Second, ... Third, ... Fourth, ...', numbered or lettered items such as i) ii) iii) or 1) 2), and explicit roadmap sentences announcing what the paper will do in order. Score 0 when contributions are stated in flowing prose with no enumeration; score 5 when there is one ordinal sequence or a single 'we make two contributions' announcement; score 10 when the body of the abstract is organised as an explicit numbered list. Score only how much of this scaffolding is visible. The judge must NOT decide whether the enumerated contributions are substantial, whether the organisation aids the reader, or whether enumerating is good scientific practice.
candidates.upstream_parent: the authors' accumulated practice in this submission format; rubric-aware, reviewer-facing writing habits learned over repeated submission cycles

candidates.criterion: Named large-scale computing infrastructure or hardware mentions
candidates.instruction: On a 0-10 scale, rate how much the text names specific large-scale or branded computing infrastructure, hardware, or vendor platforms (e.g. a named cloud TPU/GPU pod, a named trusted-hardware enclave, a named corporate code namespace) as part of describing the experiments. Score only the presence/specificity of such named infrastructure mentions; do NOT judge whether that infrastructure was necessary or whether the resulting research is good.

Score 10 if the paper proposes complex, fine-grained mechanisms for dynamically routing or mixing information between specific architectural sub-components (e.g., layers, image regions). Score 0 if it uses standard, monolithic end-to-end processing.
